name: Rely-Guarantee Reasoning Constraint (Jones)
description: cvc5 SMT verification of rely-guarantee compatibility in concurrent programs

pytorch.reason: pytorch not needed; pure symbolic/algebraic computation via cvc5 and sympy

pyg.reason: PyG message passing not needed; logic constraints handled via SMT solver

z3.reason: z3 not needed; cvc5 handles all SMT constraint proofs in this sim

cvc5.reason: load_bearing SMT verification of rely-guarantee compatibility

sympy.reason: sympy: supportive symbolic algebra for stability conditions

clifford.reason: Clifford algebra not needed; rely-guarantee constraints only

geomstats.reason: geomstats not needed; no differential geometry in this sim

e3nn.reason: e3nn not needed; no SO(3) equivariance required

rustworkx.reason: rustworkx not needed; no graph structure in this sim

xgi.reason: xgi not needed; pairwise interactions only

toponetx.reason: toponetx not needed; standard algebraic ops sufficient

gudhi.reason: gudhi not needed; no persistent homology in this sim

test_1_compatible_contracts.description: Programs with compatible G1⊆R2 and G2⊆R1 contracts

test_2_overlapping_guarantees.description: Program 1 guarantees [0,50) compatible with Program 2 relying on [0,100)

test_3_stability_condition.description: Stability: precondition x≥0 preserved under rely on y

test_1_incompatible_guarantee.description: Program 1 guarantees [0,20) but Program 2 relies on [0,10) -- incompatible

test_2_mutual_incompatibility.description: Program 1 guarantees [15,25) but Program 2 relies on [10,20) -- incompatible

test_3_stability_violated.description: Precondition x>0 violated by rely that sets x to -1
